races.name: Joe Mac's Big Retirement Bash Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jura
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old has a solid record on good ground at similar trips, but a string of mid-pack finishes in recent runs and a [STYLE_FIT] flag — noting it races somewhat out of role in the pace-setter position — means its chance depends on the tempo being entirely on its own terms, which is plausible here but no guarantee of a winning effort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts but was runner-up two runs back, form that keeps this filly right amongst the dangers on our figures. Race-fit just six days on with today's distance already covered, but fifth last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Nightsinwhitesatin
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's lightly raced four-year-old boasts a remarkable consistency record — all five recent runs on good or soft ground have returned top-two finishes at 12f — and with Cian Horgan (5lb claim) aboard and headgear fitted, the horse is well positioned in-role to track Spirit Of Jura and execute a straightforward tactical race.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score but the model of consistency, with four runner-up efforts in its last five starts around one modest fourth. That regularity underpins a clear rating edge in this small field, fit again seven days on with today's distance already proven.

runners_data.name: Rizal
runners_data.note: George Scott's runner arrives on the back of a recent win and a second, showing improved form, but the key context is that his natural pace-committed style has been redistributed to the rear for this analysis simply due to field composition — in reality, Tudhope may well elect to push forward and race prominently, which could unsettle the expected dynamic considerably.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and despite ranking only third of three on our figures, that success keeps this gelding among the dangers. A 21-day break since is the one concern, though placed efforts either side of a blip three starts back show solid, consistent form.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Of Jura is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner field, holding the prominent role and likely to set a measured, uncontested gallop over the 1m4f trip at Hamilton. Nightsinwhitesatin has the profile to track closely from a prominent position, meaning the front two will essentially race in tandem from early on, while Rizal — a natural prominent type redistributed to the back due to the field's composition — will likely be asked to settle further back than is natural for him. With no genuine hold-up horse and no rival to force a contested pace, Spirit Of Jura should control fractions entirely on its own terms, creating a steady, sustainable tempo rather than a searching gallop. This shape strongly favours prominent-racing types who can glide into contention without expending energy, rewarding horses that can race handily and produce their effort from a short distance out — making Nightsinwhitesatin's in-role positioning the most tactically advantaged profile. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural forward position; Spirit Of Jura and Nightsinwhitesatin are most likely to actually hold those berths, with Rizal forced to accommodate further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Front Two Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Jura controls a genuine but unhurried gallop and Nightsinwhitesatin tracks closely throughout, the race becomes a test of quality and fitness rather than tactics.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Jura dictates from the front without pressure, and Nightsinwhitesatin — consistently placed at similar trips on good ground — can simply shadow and outfinish its rival in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Rizal Finishes Past Both
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly slow enough that Rizal, forced to settle last, gets a soft lead to close into and produces a late burst.
scenarios.body: Rizal's recent win over 10f on good ground shows finishing pace, and a falsely run race might bring that into play even from an out-of-role position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Spirit Of Jura Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Jura is allowed such an uncontested lead that it simply steals the race and is never reeled in over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With no horse applying early pressure, Charlie Johnston's runner could exploit a lethargic tempo to build an unassailable advantage, particularly if Nightsinwhitesatin is ridden conservatively.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Gruelling Finish, All Compact
scenarios.trigger: If Hamilton's undulations and an unexpectedly demanding pace string the field out and the race is decided by who stays best to the line.
scenarios.body: An unlikely scenario with only three runners and no confirmed pacemaker forcing a strong gallop, but Nightsinwhitesatin's strong stamina profile over 12f repeatedly on good ground would suit a stamina-test finish.

watchPoints.text: Rizal's jockey Daniel Tudhope may ignore the redistributed map position entirely and push forward early, which would transform the pace dynamic from a solo-led affair into a contested front if he clashes with Spirit Of Jura.

Nightsinwhitesatin carries headgear (p) and has run consistently at 12f but steps up to 14f today — watch whether Cian Horgan allows the horse to bowl along close to Spirit Of Jura or drops in conservatively, as the trip extension is an unknown.

Spirit Of Jura's last five runs show only one placing in five efforts, and despite controlling the pace in this field, its finishing kick has been limited — watch if it capitulates once challenged in the final furlong.

With only three runners and going listed as unknown at Hamilton, any significant change in surface conditions could disproportionately affect horses at the heavier end of the weights — Spirit Of Jura carries 134lbs, the highest burden in the field.

races.name: Jordan Electrics EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands A, B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Hamish MacGregor Memorial Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Recent 6f winner on Good ground for Tim Easterby, in excellent course-applicable form (3W in last 5, sim-going 4/5), wears headgear and is the natural pace-setter here; STYLE_FIT tag is a mild caution that she can overreach her lead role if tested, but in a field of five with no genuine challenger she should dictate fully.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner two starts back, form that makes this filly a leading threat on our figures. Fit 24 days on with today's distance covered, though it only ranks third of five here.

runners_data.name: Brandenburg
runners_data.note: David Egan partners a horse that has won over 5f on Soft and placed on Good — the step to 6f is the key question; a natural prominent racer whose true front-ranking tendencies are squeezed out by superior front-runners in this shape, so it will likely race further back than ideal, blunting its best chance.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, and a winner two starts back; our figures make this colt a leading threat here. Race-fit after six days with today's trip proven, though he was unplaced three starts back.

runners_data.name: Quiet Soul
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's hold-up type has placed twice from three runs and goes on Good ground, but steps up 1f to 6f here; in a slowly-run small field it faces the hardest task of all deep closers, needing the pace to capitulate in the final furlong to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of its last three starts, including runner-up three starts back, and clear the best on our figures here. Fit again after a 35-day break, with today's trip proven; only the below-form effort last time offers a slight note of caution.

runners_data.name: Beauty For Love
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston representative who has recorded no wins and only one place in similar-going form (2/3 sim-going), and whose hold-up style is best served by a strong gallop this race is unlikely to produce; Daniel Muscutt's experience helps, but the tactical set-up looks unfavourable.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in its last three starts, sixth last time out following a modest third and a seventh before that. Bottom of five on our figures, but it is race-fit just 14 days on and already has today's distance covered.

runners_data.name: Tango Hotel
runners_data.note: Runs just one day after its last start — a significant freshness flag — yet arrives with a recent win (1/5f/SOF) and a prominent style that maps naturally onto covering Fern Clyde; Daniel Tudhope is adept in small fields, and if the quick turnaround has no ill effect this is the most plausible challenger to the leader.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, just a day ago, and a winner two starts back; this filly rates a real threat on our figures. The very quick turnaround is the main risk, though today's trip is proven.

races.paceDynamic: Fern Clyde is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only Tango Hotel and Brandenburg as rivals for prominent positions, she should stride to the front unchallenged from the outset and control a measured, unhurried gallop over Hamilton's undulating 6f. Tango Hotel arrives just one day after its last run yet carries headgear and a prominent style, and with Brandenburg also a genuine up-with-pace type — more prominent types exist than this small field can naturally absorb — Fern Clyde is most likely to secure the rail and dictate. The field contains more pace-inclined runners than can all get their preferred spot, with Fern Clyde and Tango Hotel best placed to hold the front two berths while Brandenburg is effectively pushed further back than suits. A single, uncontested pace-setter controlling a small five-runner field over a flat 6f strongly favours horses tracking that lead closely — prominent to midfield-tracking profiles who can pounce at the two-furlong pole hold the clearest positional advantage, while deep hold-up horses face the most ground to make up with little cover and a limited pace injection to chase.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fern Clyde Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Fern Clyde dictates a measured gallop and kicks clear entering the final furlong before hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: Fern Clyde's recent 1/6f/GOO win on similar ground and prominent style fit a lone-leader scenario perfectly; with no genuine rival to press her, she sets an honest but not brutal tempo and her stamina holds firm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tango Hotel tracks Fern Clyde closely and launches off the pace turning in, picking her off in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Tango Hotel has won over 5f on Good and Soft and steps up to 6f with a prominent style that suits covering the leader; Daniel Tudhope's tactical acuity in small fields makes this runner a credible threat to overhaul a front-runner who has used energy in front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and Quiet Soul or Beauty For Love close strongly from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Quiet Soul and Beauty For Love both hold deep hold-up profiles and would need an unusually strong early pace to reel in a composed front-runner in a five-runner field; the small field size and lack of pace pressure makes a genuine late-closers scenario unlikely, as the gallop is unlikely to be fast enough to bring them into it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Early Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses contest the lead aggressively early, burning pace and opening the race up for hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Brandenburg's redistribution means it may be shuffled back and forced to race without cover, creating brief early friction; however with only five runners and a clear natural leader in Fern Clyde, a sustained scrappy pace contest is the least likely shape of all.

watchPoints.text: Tango Hotel ran only yesterday — monitor market moves and any overnight scratching news, as a one-day turnaround in a 2yo nursery is an unusual training decision that could indicate a bold yard gamble or a suitability concern.

Brandenburg's natural pace means it may try to push forward early despite being mapped to midfield — watch for a fractious break or a push for position in the first furlong that could disrupt Fern Clyde's uncontested lead.

Fern Clyde is the clear pace-setter but has a STYLE_FIT flag — if she races greener than usual or is slow away, the tactical picture changes entirely as there is no secondary horse to take up the running cleanly.

With only five runners and three prominent-style horses, the first two furlongs will determine whether this is a truly solo lead or a contested pace — watch the early positioning closely as it frames every scenario.

races.name: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ferrous
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a 6f Sandown course record that won't replicate here — Hamilton's straight 6f suits front-end runners, and his 3/15 strike rate on similar ground underscores limited relevance in this shape; Callum Rodriguez will be patient but faces a big ask from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a solid second four outings back among modest efforts, but he has raced over today's distance and returns quickly after just 20 days off. Our figure rates him well clear of his 97 official mark, underpinning today's confidence.

runners_data.name: Commanche Falls
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: a confirmed front-runner returning from 148 days off for Michael Dods, whose 3/29 recent trainer form is modest, but the key asset here is positional control — excellent 10/15 similar-going record, blinkers on, and Mark Winn simply has to keep it simple.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts in his last five starts and previous experience over today's trip give him claims here, and he tops our figures for this race. The obvious concern is fitness following a 148-day break.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's veteran 10-year-old is a true hold-up horse by nature — the midfield mapping reflects a crowded pace end rather than his actual preference, and a [STYLE_FIT] flag tempers confidence that he can recapture ground he won't naturally have; fades in finish is a significant concern over 6f.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, but our figure rates him well above his 84 official mark, with previous experience over today's distance and a quick return just 11 days after his latest outing. A well-beaten eighth last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 6f/good combination at Carlisle recently and is a natural prominent racer by inclination — squeezed toward midfield on the map only because this field runs heavier up front than normal; Tim Easterby's yard is firing (8/73) and the headgear (t) is stable gear.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and returns quickly here just 11 days later, with previous experience over today's distance. Even so, our figure has him down among the outsiders for this field, some way behind the leading contenders today.

runners_data.name: Sir Garfield
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 6f/good winners for John & Sean Quinn and a horse who wants to be prominent — the redistribution simply reflects too many similar types, not a change in his natural approach; Jason Hart on a 4W/6P horse over the right trip is a strong profile, style-fit flag noted.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins in his last two starts catch the eye, and he has previous experience over today's distance, but our figure rates him bottom of this field and some way below his 80 official mark. Big form questions remain despite that recent upturn.

runners_data.name: Gangsta Man
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners a four-year-old with a 3W/4P record on good ground and who won over 5f/good at Carlisle — Jim Goldie's yard is active and this horse's prominent style is naturally suited to sitting second or third behind Commanche Falls on a track that rewards that position.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out following a mixed sequence of finishes, and races again quickly here 22 days later with experience over today's trip. Our figure rates him below his 90 official mark, leaving questions on balance.

runners_data.name: Strike Red
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's eight-year-old won over 6f/good at Carlisle in recent form and is a proven prominent type — 7/15 on similar going is the weakest statistical fit in the field, and Billy Garritty will need the pace to develop in a way that maximises a late prominent push.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and quick to return here after 20 days off, with experience over today's distance. He's shown some flat efforts further back in that sequence, though our figure edges him a couple of pounds above his 88 official mark.

runners_data.name: Saint Lawrence
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's hold-up specialist with headgear (blinkers) and Kevin Stott aboard, but a 5/15 similar-going record and 41 days since last run are both flags — a true rear-seated runner who needs a strong gallop to bring him into play, and this race may not supply it.
runners_data.comment: A solid second two starts back shows ability, and our figure rates him well clear of his 85 official mark. He's winless in his last five starts, and the yard is out of form, striking at just 4% over the last 14 days - the main worry today.

races.paceDynamic: Commanche Falls is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push him from the gates, he should secure an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop over this 6f Hamilton straight. The pace dynamic is essentially a single-setter scenario — Gangsta Man and Strike Red are prominent types who will track rather than challenge for the lead, meaning Commanche Falls can control tempo and dictate a measured, even pace. Several runners — Sir Garfield, Manila Scouse, and Jordan Electrics — are genuine prominent or hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural position given the compression of styles across this eight-runner field; of those, Sir Garfield and Manila Scouse are the most likely to actually push forward and land close to the pace, while Jordan Electrics will be forced wider or further back than ideal. A controlled, single-paced 6f on good ground at Hamilton favours prominent racers who can slot in behind the leader and sprint from two out — pure hold-up horses asking from the rear face the steepest task.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Commanche Falls Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Commanche Falls leads uncontested and sets a comfortable, even tempo that keeps the race honest without burning them off.
scenarios.body: Commanche Falls controls the race from the front at a gallop that suits his confirmed front-running style, giving himself every chance to outstay a field that must work to peg him back; prominent trackers sitting second and third have the ideal trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to set up a late run from the chasing prominent group, with the winner landing from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Gangsta Man or Strike Red track Commanche Falls at close range and use a sustained finish from two out to wear him down on the run to the line; this shape suits horses who can press the pace without being swamped early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or stalls early, creating a false-pace scenario that compresses the field and allows rear-seated runners to get competitive.
scenarios.body: Ferrous or Saint Lawrence, both genuine hold-up types, get into contention if the gallop is insufficient to stretch the field; this scenario requires a pace mishap that is unlikely given Commanche Falls's confirmed lead style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Commanche Falls sets a too-slow pace and the race degenerates into a sprint from the three-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A stop-start tempo creates a bunched cavalry charge in the final two furlongs, where shorter-priced prominent types with finishing pace hold an edge; this shape is the least supported by the available evidence.

watchPoints.text: Commanche Falls has been off for 148 days — monitor whether he shows any signs of ring-rustiness at the start or is keen early, as either would materially alter the pace map.

Sir Garfield and Manila Scouse are both natural prominent types who cannot both get their preferred spot — watch the early break to see which one pushes forward and which is forced to settle, as that resolves Scenario B vs D.

Jordan Electrics is tagged as fading in the finish and is racing out of role — if the field compresses mid-race and he is shuffled back further than the midfield map shows, his chance effectively disappears.

Gangsta Man's record at 5f/good (1W) versus 6f/good (4th last time) warrants attention — if he tracks Commanche Falls comfortably to the two-furlong pole, his staying power over this trip is the critical unknown that determines Scenario A or B.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Glasgow Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Mr Colonel
runners_data.note: Shane Gray takes the ride for the Fahey yard, and his sim-going record (5/6 runs on good or similar) is solid, but the most recent outing was a distant 9th over 14f on good — this hold-up specialist is entirely dependent on Prizeland blowing up, which a lone leader in a small field rarely does.
runners_data.comment: A game winner three starts back, he tops our figures here and holds a 3lb edge over his official mark, with previous experience over today's trip. Only a below-par ninth last time out, after a 30-day break, counts against him.

runners_data.name: Superior Choice
runners_data.note: Two wins from three runs on good ground show real class for a horse rated OR 87, and the Gosden handler's 7/16 14-day strike rate is the strongest in this field — his natural style is to race prominently, and he will struggle to find that berth freely given the congestion ahead of him.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins in his last two starts read well on paper, and he has previous experience over today's trip. But our figure rates him bottom of this field and some way below his 87 official mark, leaving obvious questions to answer at this level.

runners_data.name: Flawless Fusion
runners_data.note: Jessica Bedi's yard is 0/4 in the 14-day window and the horse's most recent run — 10th of 10 on good ground — is a sharp concern; she wants to race prominently by nature but the field is too packed at the front for her to land that pitch, and her OR 74 marks her as the class anchor of this race.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts in her last five starts show she has some ability, and our figure has her some way above her 74 official mark. But she's winless in that sequence, and a 46-day absence adds to the questions.

runners_data.name: Folk Pageant
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's operation is firing (7/66 in 14 days) and this horse arrives just seven days after a run, suggesting the stable is deliberately targeting this spot; two wins from five on good ground over 10f, and a prominent style that genuinely fits the one position available just off Prizeland, makes the fitness-and-style combo compelling.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last six starts underline solid ability, and a rapid return here just seven days after her latest outing keeps her sharp, with previous experience over today's trip. A below-par sixth last time out is the obvious knock.

runners_data.name: Plaid
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's runner has a respectable sim-going record (2/5 on good or similar) and won twice over 8f before stepping up in trip, but his front-running tendencies will be frustrated by Prizeland's prior claim on the lead — racing further back than he wants will blunt his finishing effort in the straight.
runners_data.comment: A striking record of two wins and two runner-up efforts across her last four starts came before a below-par fifth last time out. Our figure still has her 3lb above her 89 official mark, though a 40-day absence since that run is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Prizeland
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's operation is the most active in this field at 11/55 in 14 days, and Prizeland holds a clear tactical trump card as the only confirmed front-runner — his recent win over 12f on standard and placed effort at 12f on good shows the trip is within range, and an uncontested lead on the long Hamilton straight could prove decisive.
runners_data.comment: Two wins and a runner-up effort across three starts before a below-par fifth last time out leave her second on our figures, with previous experience over today's trip and a 2lb edge over her 94 official mark. That recent fifth, 26 days back, is the one blot.

races.paceDynamic: Prizeland is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him into a fast early tempo, P J McDonald can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over 1m3f at Hamilton. Folk Pageant is the likeliest horse to sit closest in second from the prominent berth, giving the race a clean, processional shape rather than a contested, lung-burning pace. The field contains more genuine prominent types than can physically hold that position — Plaid, Superior Choice, and Flawless Fusion all want to race up with or near the pace but will inevitably be shuffled into a midfield role they are not naturally comfortable in, compromising their chances in any shape that requires them to be held up and produce a late run. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a measured gallop on good turf — strongly favours horses capable of racing prominently or tracking the pace efficiently and finishing cleanly, rather than true hold-up horses who need a stronger tempo to generate momentum; Mr Colonel, as the sole genuine hold-up runner, is the one who depends most on the pace being quick enough to set up a meaningful late effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prizeland Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Prizeland is allowed to dictate an unchallenged, even gallop and the field never seriously tests him before the straight.
scenarios.body: Prizeland sets fractions he fully controls through the long Hamilton straight, and with Folk Pageant's recent winners' form over 10f on good giving him the fitness edge to track and possibly overhaul, the race is run entirely to the front-runners' script.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Swoops Late Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Prizeland's pace is slightly quicker than it looks early and one prominent tracker finds extra in the Hamilton straight.
scenarios.body: The long run-in at Hamilton suits a horse who has been sitting a length or two off the pace in a rhythm and has fuel left when Prizeland begins to tie up — Superior Choice's class (two wins on good ground) and the Gosden stable's recent 7/16 14-day form give him the profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Squeezed Prominents Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace causes the redistributed prominent horses to take their natural position anyway, creating a bunched tactical affair settled by raw class.
scenarios.body: With Plaid, Superior Choice, and Flawless Fusion all wanting to race prominently, a crowded mid-pack develops and the horse with the highest class ceiling — Superior Choice at OR 87 on an upward trajectory — benefits from a slowly-run race that rewards quality over position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Prizeland sets a truly strong pace that collapses in the straight, opening a late window for Mr Colonel.
scenarios.body: Mr Colonel has form figures of 1W3P on similar good ground and clearly has ability, but this scenario requires a pace collapse that a single uncontested front-runner on 1m3f is very unlikely to engineer; his recent 9th from a hold-up position over further suggests trip and tempo risks remain.

watchPoints.text: Prizeland's early positioning is critical — if Folk Pageant or Plaid break sharply and push him into a contested early pace, the scenario probabilities shift materially toward hold-up types.

Superior Choice is racing out of his natural prominent role due to traffic ahead of him; watch how quickly Shane Foley can find a clear path and whether he gets trapped wide burning energy on the turn.

Folk Pageant's seven-day turnaround looks deliberate, but if the horse is not at peak freshness after six outings including two wins, his ability to sustain a tracking effort through the 1m3f trip could fade in the final two furlongs.

Mr Colonel is fitted with headgear (hg:t) and is the only true hold-up runner in the field — if Prizeland sets even a marginally stronger pace than expected, watch whether Shane Gray drops him out early or tries to sit closer to exploit any tempo increase.

Flawless Fusion's trainer has 0 winners from 4 runners in the 14-day window and her OR 74 is well below the rest — she represents the lowest-probability runner in any scenario but could disrupt the pace dynamic if she breaks faster than expected from the gate.

races.name: Hamilton Park Celebrates 100 Years Of Racing Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Law Of Average
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form — two wins in last four runs over 5f — and Joey Haynes has strong recent form, but this hold-up profile is most vulnerable in a race set to be run at a modest tempo off Rock Of England's lead; has good form on similar going but must produce a big finish.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, his third success in five starts, and quickly backs up here just 11 days later with previous experience over today's trip. Our figure has him 8lb clear of his 81 official mark, making him the one to beat on these figures.

runners_data.name: Justmyluck
runners_data.note: A 55-day absence raises a fitness question, and Linda Perratt's trainer strike rate of 0/16 in the past 14 days tempers confidence; the hold-up style is also unlikely to be ideally suited by the controlled pace, and limited course form (sim-going record 0W0P) adds further caution.|
runners_data.comment: A winning effort four starts back hints at ability, but the three runs since have been below that level, with a below-par eighth last time out. Our figure matches his 73 official mark exactly, and a 55-day absence adds to the fitness question.

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Quick back after just four days, and Greg Fairley takes over; the horse's natural style is hold-up, but with the field producing more closers than the shape can accommodate, it will find itself racing from a midfield position that does not reflect its instincts — sim-going record of 1W1P from 15 runs on comparable ground is modest.|
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is the highlight of an otherwise mixed sequence, and he's fresh from a run just four days ago with previous experience over today's trip. Even so, our figure has him bottom of this five-runner field today.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Uncontested front-runner here with a strong record at this course and distance — two wins on Good ground — and the position of leader in a race with no likely challenger for that slot is a significant tactical asset; the STYLE_FIT flag suggests a slight positional drift from pure role, but in practice he is ideally placed.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and with two wins earlier in this five-start sequence, he returns quickly here 11 days later with previous experience over today's trip. Our figure already has him 8lb above his 72 official mark, so the question is whether there's more improvement left to find.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's stable is in excellent form (6/67 T14) and Paul Mulrennan is a shrewd judge of pace; the prominent style sits naturally in the slipstream of Rock Of England, and a sim-going record of 4W8P from 13 runs is comfortably the strongest in the field on comparable ground — consistent second-place finishes suggest it shows up without always winning.|
runners_data.comment: Three runner-up efforts in her last six starts show she goes well without quite getting her head in front, and she's fresh from a run just four days ago with previous experience over today's trip. Our figure has her 6lb above her 70 official mark, though she remains without a win.

races.paceDynamic: Rock Of England is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, Jason Hart can dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the front over this 5f at Hamilton. Woohoo will likely slot in behind as a prominent racer, giving Rock Of England a small shadow but no real challenge for the lead, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. The hold-up trio — Law Of Average, Justmyluck, and Jm Jhingree — will need to make ground from off the pace, though Jm Jhingree is a redistributed runner whose natural style is hold-up but has been mapped to midfield given the field composition, meaning it will not occupy a true stalking role naturally. This race shape, with a lone uncontested leader setting a comfortable tempo, strongly favours prominent or pace-pressing profiles that can travel close to the action and pounce without needing a strong end-to-end gallop to bring them into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rock Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Of England leads uncontested and sets a sustainable pace, the horse travelling prominently behind him lands the knockout blow.
scenarios.body: Rock Of England dictates from the front at a measured tempo, with Woohoo pressing close enough to challenge from the two-pole home; a steady gallop fails to stretch the field enough for the hold-up horses to reel in the leaders. Prominent profiles who can press or respond to the leader's rhythm without burning petrol are the primary beneficiaries of this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Steals It Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so comfortable that Rock Of England simply bowls along and no challenger has the gears to reel him in late.
scenarios.body: Rock Of England, untroubled on the front end, conserves energy through a sedate tempo and quickens away in the final furlong before the hold-up horses can mount a challenge; Jason Hart's positional advantage becomes decisive on a track where ground is hard to make up. This suits a horse able to both lead and find more under pressure, and Rock Of England's course-and-distance record of two wins on Good ground underlines his suitability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than anticipated and the leaders tie up, allowing a hold-up performer to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Should something quicken the early gallop and the front end emptied out late, a closer with a strong finishing run could pick up the pieces; Law Of Average is the most credible candidate given recent wins on similar ground and over this trip. However, the pace dynamics offer little encouragement for this shape — Rock Of England is unlikely to be pressed hard enough to leave the door truly open for closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are misjudged, the field concertinas and an unexpected challenger emerges from a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo could see the race turn into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, compressing the field and giving every runner a fighting chance in the final stages; Jm Jhingree, despite being a redistributed hold-up type and out of natural role, could theoretically benefit if the pace sets up for a late burst. This is an unlikely scenario given Rock Of England's front-running profile and Hart's ability to control the tempo.

watchPoints.text: Rock Of England and Woohoo — if Hart eases the tempo significantly at the halfway point, Mulrennan on Woohoo is well-positioned to pounce before the hold-up horses can respond, making this pairing the critical tactical battle to watch from the front.

Law Of Average — Joey Haynes will need to produce a strong late run from off the pace, but a slow or moderate tempo set by Rock Of England could leave insufficient ground to make up in the final furlong; watch whether the pace is genuinely testing enough to bring the closer into play.

Justmyluck — a 55-day absence combined with a 0/16 trainer strike rate over the past fortnight introduces a notable fitness unknown; watch paddock demeanour and early running to assess whether the horse is tuned up for a return after nearly eight weeks off.

Jm Jhingree — back after only four days and racing out of natural style by occupying a midfield rather than true hold-up position; watch whether Fairley opts to push forward early to compensate or settles for a compromised berth that leaves the horse needing an unlikely late turn of foot.

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse with good similar-going form (1 win, 3 places from 13 runs on good), but the crowded rear of this field means Paul Mulrennan may be forced wider and closer to the pace than ideal; the style-fit discount applies here — racing out of its natural hold-up role tempers confidence, though the class ceiling is the highest in the race.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out; also runner-up three starts back, and a winner five starts back, with previous form over today's trip. Our figure has her 7lb above her 69 official mark, a leading threat back after 22 days off.

runners_data.name: Sogniamo
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old carries the strongest win credentials of the hold-up group — a course-type winner on good ground with Daniel Tudhope booked — but only three career runs limit the form sample; the 28-day break should have freshened her, and if she can find a clean run from whatever position she settles, she is the most likely closer to make an impact.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is sandwiched between two well-beaten efforts, and our figure has her bottom of this field, some way below her 70 official mark. The yard is out of form too, striking at just 4% in its last 14 days, leaving obvious question marks.

runners_data.name: Zermatt Star
runners_data.note: Returning from a 67-day absence with a flat recent form line (0 wins, 0 places in last four on similar going) and a new training partnership of Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood with a modest 14-day strike rate; naturally a hold-up type who will drift to the rear, and in a race with limited pace to close onto, the stiff task of hitting top form first time out after a lengthy break makes her hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Modest recent form with no better than fifth in her last four starts, but our figure still rates her above her 69 official mark, and she has previous experience over today's trip. A 67-day absence is the biggest concern, leaving her fitness today an open question.

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's veteran mare brings solid recent form (placed twice in five starts on good ground) and ran just six days ago, indicating she is right in the firing line of fitness; the prominent style means she will track Stella Lucente and is the most likely horse to apply any semblance of pressure, though she lacks the raw ability to make a sustained challenge for supremacy.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and third two starts back, fourth three starts back, with previous form over today's trip and a quick six-day turnaround. She remains without a win, though our figure edges her above her 61 official mark.

runners_data.name: Stella Lucente
runners_data.note: The only front-runner in the race, Callum Rodriguez takes a straightforward brief to lead and dictate on this flat 1m½f track; consistent placed form including two second-place finishes on good ground confirms she handles conditions, and the hood (headgear) suggests she needs to be kept focused — controlling the race from the front suits that requirement perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Placed in all of her last five starts - three times runner-up, twice third - she tops our figures here, 9lb clear of her 67 official mark. She's quick to return after just 11 days, with previous experience over today's trip, yet to win in that sequence.

races.paceDynamic: Stella Lucente is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and will stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over 1m½f at Hamilton, setting a controlled, sustainable tempo with no rival capable of — or likely to — press her early. The three hold-up types (Geo, Sogniamo, Zermatt Star) will track from behind, with Second Fiddle the only other runner likely to sit close to the pace in a prominent position, though without the natural pace instinct to threaten Stella Lucente for the lead. With no pace pressure, Stella Lucente can dictate rhythm and conserve energy, making this a race where the leader has maximum opportunity to control sectionals and potentially steal a decisive advantage. This race shape most clearly favours the front-running profile: an uncontested, well-managed lead at a flat, galloping track with no natural pressure is a significant tactical asset, and hold-up runners will need the pace to be strong enough to close — conditions that do not look guaranteed here. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than can all achieve their preferred rear-tracking positions, and among Geo, Sogniamo, and Zermatt Star, Geo and Sogniamo are most likely to secure the closest tracking berths given their form and rider quality.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lucente Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Stella Lucente sets an unchallenged, measured gallop and holds enough in reserve to repel challengers turning in.
scenarios.body: Stella Lucente dictates every yard of the race from the front, controlling the tempo on a flat track with no rival willing to commit and pressure her early; with energy banked through the middle stages, she is ideally placed to kick clear when challengers make their move in the straight. This shape rewards the front-running profile entirely, and Stella Lucente's consistent placed form around this type of trip and going confirms she stays the distance when allowed to bowl along on her own terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Stella Lucente sets a genuinely fast early pace that causes her to fade in the final two furlongs, opening the door for closers.
scenarios.body: With a lead set at a sharp clip from the front, the hold-up horses tracking midfield have enough time and space on the Hamilton straight to close the gap; Sogniamo, a winner over this sort of going and with Daniel Tudhope in the saddle, is the most credible beneficiary given her single-race win profile. Geo has the class and similar-going form to finish into a place if the pace does collapse, though having been redistributed from a true hold-up position, its ability to get into the ideal tracking spot is not guaranteed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to stretch the field but Second Fiddle tracks Stella Lucente closely and outstays her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Second Fiddle, with prominent-style credentials and useful recent placed form on good ground, could sit just off the pace and inherit the advantage if Stella Lucente runs out of fuel; the mare's consistency in this grade and her very recent run (6 days ago) suggest she is fit and primed. The longer 1m½f trip at a flat Hamilton track suits a horse who grinds rather than quickens, and a well-judged Cara Tuke ride could make this work.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Muddled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses all fail to get their preferred positions and the race devolves into a messy, slowly-run affair with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: With three horses naturally wanting to race from the rear but unable to all secure ideal ground, bunching in midfield creates a fractious, stop-start dynamic that suits no one cleanly; any runner who avoids traffic and produces a clear run late could snatch an unlikely result. Zermatt Star, returning from 67 days off and with limited recent form, remains the most opaque runner and could outperform expectations if the race falls apart at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Stella Lucente must be watched in the opening two furlongs — if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged at a comfortable tempo, she converts this into a front-runner's procession and the hold-up brigade will have insufficient pace to close onto.

Geo and Sogniamo are both natural hold-up horses trying to occupy the same limited rear ground; watch for interference or blocked runs in the straight if both attempt to switch outside simultaneously with only five runners spread across the track.

Second Fiddle's very recent run (6 days ago) is a double-edged sword — if the mare shows signs of bounce effect and fades early, the pace structure collapses entirely and the race shape becomes chaotic for the hold-up runners who need something to chase.

Zermatt Star's 67-day absence and poor recent record on good ground makes her the most likely to drift early and lose contact; if she is quickly detached, the effective race becomes a four-horse contest and Stella Lucente's lead becomes even more comfortable than the small field suggests.
